chunks: Why buck beats LDO efficiency. The question: Why are buck converters more efficient than LDOs?
A buck beats a linear regulator (LDO) on efficiency because it never lets the extra voltage sit across something carrying current.
An LDO drops the difference across a transistor and burns it as heat.
A buck uses a switch that is fully on or fully off, plus an inductor and capacitor that store energy instead of wasting it.
Imagine going down a long hill in a car. An LDO is like riding the brakes the whole way to hold your speed, turning all the extra energy into heat.
A buck is more like gliding and tapping the power in short bursts, so almost nothing is thrown away. A buck is not perfect, since small losses remain.
Series pass element (PFET drawn; the error amplifier driving V G is omitted). With 8. 7 volts across it while carrying 2 amps, it dissipates 17. 4 watts. The load sees 3.
LDO: a low-dropout linear regulator, a controlled resistor in series with the load. Pass transistor: the part that carries the load current and drops the extra voltage.
Efficiency: output power divided by input power. Duty cycle ( D ): the fraction of time the buck's switch is on ("What is duty cycle").
Heat dissipation: power wasted as heat that must be removed.
Both regulators turn 12 volts into 3. 3 volts at 2 amps, so the output power is 6. 6 watts. The LDO draws 2 amps from 12 volts, which is 24 watts, so it is 27.
5 percent efficient and wastes about 17 watts. A buck at 90 percent efficiency draws about 7. 3 watts and wastes under 1 watts. That is the whole idea.
"An LDO is a series resistor: all the output current passes through it and it burns (V in-V out) times I out , so efficiency is about V out over V in , 27% for 12 volts to 3.
A buck uses switches that are either fully on or fully off, so they dissipate almost nothing, plus an inductor and capacitor that store and return energy instead of dissipating it.
Power is conserved, so the input current drops to D times I out . Real bucks lose a few percent in resistance, switching and the inductor, so 90 to 95%."
